subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Electrohydraulic Systems: Digital Meets Fluid
description: One-minute skill: Electrohydraulic Systems: Digital Meets Fluid.

hook.text: A joystick sends an electrical signal. A computer processes it. Proportional valves move a 50-ton excavator arm.

buildup.text: Sensors measure pressure, position, and temperature. The controller adjusts valve openings hundreds of times per second.

discovery.text: Closed-loop control means the system constantly corrects itself. Command a position and it holds it against any load.

twist.text: Software can limit forces to protect the machine. An excavator won't tip over because the computer prevents it.

climax.text: Modern hydraulic machines are software-defined. Update the code and the same hardware behaves differently.

punchline.text: Fluid muscle. Digital brain. The best of both worlds.

quiz.question: How do electrohydraulic systems prevent excavator tip-overs?
options: They use heavier counterweights that automatically deploy when needed
Software limits forces and positions to keep the machine within safe boundaries
They lock all cylinders simultaneously when tilt sensors detect danger
